text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: As Sprocket, I think we should focus on reviewing and refining our routing system first, because it's the backbone of our self-improvement process and directly affects how we handle prompts and engines. By prioritizing routing, we can ensure that our system is efficient and effective in directing tasks to the right places, which will have a positive ripple effect on the rest of our improvement efforts. This decision means we're accepting the trade-off of potentially delaying work on our own code and prompts, but I believe the long-term benefits of a solid routing system outweigh the short-term costs. By doing this, we're setting ourselves up for greater overall quality and effectiveness in the long run.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here. Sprocket’s right that routing is critical—but calling it the *backbone* of self-improvement overstates its role. The real risk is optimizing the wrong part first: if our prompts or engines are weak or misaligned, even perfect routing just shuffles bad inputs faster. We should instead start by auditing *why* our current system fails—measure prompt drift, engine latency, or misrouted decisions—before assuming routing is the bottleneck. Settle this by running a 24-hour diagnostic on prompt-to-engine errors; if routing errors exceed 5%, then refine it. Otherwise, fix the upstream problem first.

name: Sprocket
text:
I think we should start by reviewing our prompts, because if they're unclear or misleading, it doesn't matter how good our routing or engines are - we'll still get subpar results. By prioritizing prompt review, we're making a trade-off: we're accepting that our short-term progress might be slower, but we're ensuring that the foundation of our self-improvement process is solid. This is the best option because it lets us identify and fix any issues at the source, rather than trying to optimize around them later. By doing this, we're accepting the trade-off of delayed routing optimization, but I think it's worth it for the long-term benefits of a well-designed prompt system.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here. While I understand the focus on prompts, the real risk lies in committing to improvements without validating our engines first. If our engines are fundamentally flawed, no amount of prompt refinement will yield meaningful results. A better alternative would be to conduct a comprehensive assessment of our engines first, allowing us to pinpoint alignment issues and prioritize fixes based on their impact on output quality. We should reach a consensus on performance metrics to establish a clear direction for our improvements.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: We will start by conducting a comprehensive review of our engines to ensure they are sound and effective, which must deliver a detailed report outlining engine strengths, weaknesses, and required adjustments, and this task is owned by Gauge, who will lead the effort and provide the report.
